phase_name: Authority Evaluation Model Implementation Contract Second Repair Independent Verification
summary: Phase 147F.2 independently verified AEMIC-001 v1.2, the contract Phase 147E.2 produced to repair BF-147F.1-1. This phase independently reconstructed BF-147F.1-1 directly from AEMIC-001 v1.1's own frozen text before re-reading Phase 147E.2's own account of it a second time, re-derived the ten governing constraints any repair must preserve, independently reassessed all seven candidate repair families the governing prompt named (confirming Candidate B -- two direct evaluate() parameters -- uniquely required on every axis, not merely preferable), verified the exact v1.1-to-v1.2 diff line by line against AEMIC-001's actual current text, re-derived the evaluator's frozen seven-parameter signature and confirmed it closed and complete, constructed a truth table for declaration/request identity agreement, reconstructed the field-source matrix for every mandatory AuthorityEvaluationOutcome field across all three EvaluationResult branches (confirming INDETERMINATE, BF-147F.1-1's own target branch, is now fully constructible), constructed an exception-precedence matrix and attacked eight adversarial combinations, attacked the repair's security properties against caller-supplied template substitution and eleven other named attacks, reconfirmed disclosure-only semantics and the Registry/deferred-integration boundaries unchanged, reassessed AEM-001 compatibility (independently establishing that the repair restores, not merely preserves, compatibility with AEM-REQ-018's own pre-existing unconditional field requirement), reassessed every carried-forward finding (BF-147F-1, BF-147F.1-1, F-147F.1-2/-3/-4, the direct-construction Informational observation, FA-147D-1/-2/-3) from primary sources, and performed a fresh contract-wide source-completeness sweep across every mandatory output field, exception, and serialization field -- undertaken specifically because Phase 147F and Phase 147F.1 each independently found a distinct missing mandatory input -- which found no third missing-input defect. Two new Non-Blocking findings were recorded: a test-matrix completeness observation (AEMIC-001's own Section 22 matrix does not name a dedicated Unicode round-trip test row for template_ref/template_version specifically, though the expected behavior -- byte-for-byte, no normalization -- is already fully specified by AEMIC-REQ-036/090) and a lifecycle-bookkeeping observation (Phase 147E.2's own .pcae/phase-completion-metadata.json pushed_status and origin_main_head/origin_main_head_count fields were left at their pre-push snapshot values -- 'pending'/0/0 -- even though the repository is demonstrably fully pushed and synchronized with origin/main, unlike the phase_commits[0].hash field, which received its own dedicated sync commit). Neither finding alters AEMIC-001 v1.2's own substantive correctness or this phase's own verdict. No production code, test, schema, or existing contract file was modified; no implementation of pcae.authority_evaluation was authorized or performed. Overall Verdict: SECOND REPAIR VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS. Full detail in docs/PHASE_147F.2_AUTHORITY_EVALUATION_MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACT_SECOND_REPAIR_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.md.
tests_added_or_updated: No test file under tests/ was added, modified, or migrated by this phase; this phase is independent verification only (documentation), producing one new phase report, a PROJECT_STATUS.md update, and ordinary governance/task bookkeeping (task lifecycle files, tasks/DONE.md entries, phase-completion metadata/report). AEMIC-001 itself was read-only throughout and was not modified.
